maya: Heads up: Deployments form review. Were debating inline validation vs a consolidated post-submit list. Also need verdict on required markers + destructive confirmation patterns. Short takes? sam: Inline for quick fixes, summary for long or multi-step flows. Hybrid could work. elaine: Hybrid sounds pragmatic: inline flags for single-field issues, banner for cross-field or summary errors after submit. Keep banner links keyboard-focusable. vik: Dev constraints: avoid big layout shifts when showing inline errors. Use smaller helper text style and aria-live="polite". For summary banners use role="alert" and include an anchor list: ````html

2 errors 0000please review

  • Quota must be a positive integer
```` jo: Accessibility: when submit triggers error summary, announce the count then move virtual focus to the banner container, not the individual field immediately. Then let users navigate to anchors. Ensure aria-invalid, aria-describedby for inline messages and avoid duplicate announcements. karen: Required marker policy: only mark required fields; use a subtle asterisk visually and add a sr-only "Required" label for screen readers. Avoid showing markers on every field. maya: Copy preference: active language helps — e.g., "Enter a cluster name" vs "This field is required". For tiny screens use short text and offer expandable hints for a11y. sam: Destructive flows: soft-delete => undo toast. Critical irreversible ops => typed confirm. For mid-risk (bulk delete many items) consider confirm checkbox + explicit count of items to be deleted. vik: Implementation for typed-confirm: require typing either a short immutable id or exact resource name. Disable the confirm until it matches. This blocks scripted accidental confirms. jo: Keyboard/mobile nuance: when focusing the first invalid field, call `element.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})` and then `element.focus()`; this avoids jarring full-page scroll on mobile. For the banner, include a "Jump to first error" button that is tabbable. karen: Deduplicate: don’t show both a toast and inline error for the same validation issue. Choose one primary channel. Toasts are good for async server failures; inline for form-level validation. maya: Governance idea: I'll draft a short doc that defines when to use each pattern (inline, banner, typed-confirm, undo). We should include examples and a table of risk thresholds. ux-bot: Figma link (maya): https://figma.com/file/mock-deploy-forms 0 0comments enabled. maya: Action items: - Elaine: refine Figma mocks (hybrid + banner) - Vik: prototype confirm modal (checkbox + typed-confirm + disabled confirm) and demo undo snackbar - Jo: write a11y checklist with recommended ARIA roles and announcement order - Sam: prepare wording variants for quick A/B on copy microcopy - Maya: draft governance doc for pattern usage and thresholds maya: Thanks — tagging reviewers. Will reconvene after prototypes are posted. :sparkles:
